g1|variants|free-of-charge delivery.summary: Free-of-charge deliveries allow businesses to ship goods to customers at no cost for promotional, sample, or replacement purposes. Variants differ based on whether a preceding sales order or quotation is required, whether billing is involved at zero value, and if the item is standard free-of-charge or a subsequent delivery for a complaint.

variants.name: Standard Free-of-Charge Order (Without Preceding Document)
variants.when_used: Used when sending promotional items, marketing samples, or goodwill gifts directly to a customer without referencing a prior commercial quotation or customer inquiry.
values: Not relevant for billing (or zero-value invoice depending on pricing setup)
variants.key_config: Sales document type FD uses item category TBN (value zero, pricing type G) and schedule line category CN, ensuring no billing document is generated while inventory is properly reduced via movement 631.

variants.name: Free-of-Charge Delivery with Quotation Reference
variants.when_used: Used for formal promotional campaigns or structured customer agreements where a quotation must be approved and converted into the free-of-charge order.
variants.key_config: Copy control from quotation type to sales order type FD is established, allowing item category TBN to flow downstream while enforcing approval checks at the quotation stage.

variants.name: Subsequent Delivery Free-of-Charge (Returns/Complaints)
variants.when_used: Used in complaint processing when goods delivered previously were defective or short-shipped, and the company agrees to send replacement goods free of charge referencing a returns order.
variants.key_config: Order type SO is created as a follow-up action from an SD quality notification or returns order, utilizing item category KLN and schedule line category DN to document the replacement.

g1|core|free-of-charge delivery|standard.title: Standard Free-of-Charge Order (Without Preceding Document)
g1|core|free-of-charge delivery|standard.story: Imagine giving away free toys at a store without making the customer pay a single penny, but keeping a record so the warehouse knows to pack them. In SAP S/4HANA, a Standard Free-of-Charge Order (Without Preceding Document) is a sales document created directly using sales document type FD that processes zero-dollar items, triggers a goods issue movement type 631, and bypasses standard customer billing. It handles promotional giveaways, marketing samples, and goodwill gestures directly within Order-to-Cash without requiring an inquiry or quotation.
g1|core|free-of-charge delivery|standard.why_business_needs_it: Companies need to ship promotional items or replacement samples to customers without generating revenue receivables or invoices, while still tracking inventory reduction and cost of goods sold. Proper configuration of document type FD and item category TBN ensures correct ledger postings to marketing or sample expense accounts instead of accounts receivable.

modules.role: Manages sales order entry using document type FD, item determination for TBN, schedule line category CN, and triggers outbound delivery creation.
modules.hands_off_to: LE (Logistics Execution) for outbound delivery creation, picking, and goods issue posting.

modules.role: Receives material valuation postings from inventory and posts the cost of the free items to a designated expense or cost center.

config_steps.step: Define Sales Document Type for Free-of-Charge Orders FD
config_steps.where: VOV8 -- SPRO > Sales and Distribution > Sales > Sales Documents > Sales Document Header > Define Sales Document Types
config_steps.values: Doc Type FD: category C, item increment 10, availability check group 02.
config_steps.check: Run VA01, enter order type FD, and verify the header accepts the creation without pricing errors.
config_steps.why: This configuration creates the specific sales document type required to process promotional giveaways and marketing samples without billing requirements.
config_steps.if_missing: If sales document type FD is missing, users cannot create free-of-charge orders, resulting in message V1002 "Sales document type FD does not exist".
actions: Enter /nVOV8 in the command field and press Enter
Select standard sales document type OR and click Copy As (F6)
Overwrite Sales Doc. Type with FD and Description with "Free-of-charge order"
Set Doc Category to C (Order)
Set Checking Group to 02
Set Item Number Incr to 10
Save (Ctrl+S) and assign a customizing transport request

config_steps.step: Define Item Categories for Free-of-Charge Orders TBN

config_steps.check: Create a sales order using item category TBN and verify that the net value is zero and no billing due list is generated.
config_steps.why: Item category TBN ensures that zero-dollar items bypass pricing and billing completely, preserving financial accuracy for promotional distributions.
config_steps.if_missing: If item category TBN is missing, free items will incorrectly generate billing due list entries and trigger unexpected customer invoices.

Select standard item category TAN and click Copy As (F6)
Overwrite Item Category with TBN and Item Category Desc with "Free w/o charge item"

g1|core|free-of-charge delivery|free-of-.story: Just like a store hands out a free sample to a shopper after checking their special coupon, a business sends complimentary goods to a customer based on a prior approved quotation without billing them. In SAP S/4HANA, this process starts when a sales order type FD is created with reference to an existing quotation, creating an outbound delivery that issues inventory using movement type 631 while keeping the billing relevance strictly non-billable.

This process ensures proper inventory tracking and cost allocation to marketing or promotional accounts while honoring the terms agreed upon in the quotation.

g1|core|free-of-charge delivery|subseque.title: Subsequent Delivery Free-of-Charge (Returns/Complaints)
g1|core|free-of-charge delivery|subseque.story: Imagine a magical store giving you an extra toy because your previous toy was broken, but making sure the receipt still says zero dollars so accounting stays happy. In SAP S/4HANA, a Subsequent Delivery Free-of-Charge creates an outbound delivery and goods issue without billing value to replace damaged goods referenced from a preceding returns order.
g1|core|free-of-charge delivery|subseque.why_business_needs_it: It maintains customer satisfaction by fulfilling warranty or complaint replacements without charging the customer, while properly tracking inventory movement and cost of goods sold in financial accounting.

modules.role: Manages the subsequent free-of-charge sales order creation referencing the returns order, pricing determination with zero value, and delivery creation.
modules.hands_off_to: LE (Logistics Execution) for picking, packing, and goods issue processing.

modules.role: Executes outbound delivery processing, picking, and posts goods issue using movement type 631.
modules.hands_off_to: FI (Financial Accounting) / CO (Controlling) for inventory posting and cost of sales.

modules.role: Posts inventory reduction and records the cost of goods delivered free of charge to expense/complaint accounts without generating a customer receivable.

g1|panel|free-of-charge delivery.otc_impact: Free-of-charge deliveries sit at the intersection of sales administration, logistics execution, and financial accounting within Order-to-Cash. This family alters standard revenue recognition by bypassing customer billing while consuming inventory and generating cost of goods sold, ultimately impacting profitability analysis and tax compliance. For orders, deliveries, and billing, it introduces specialized document types that suppress pricing elements while retaining full inventory management, picking, and delivery tracking. It integrates tightly with Finance via free-of-charge reason codes that post inventory write-offs directly to specific marketing or complaint expense accounts instead of accounts receivable.

panel_qa.question: How do we prevent sales users from accidentally granting free-of-charge status on high-value commercial orders?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: Business users require strict separation between revenue-generating sales orders and promotional or corrective free-of-charge requests. SAP enforces this via dedicated sales document types such as FD (Free-of-Charge Order) and SO (Subsequent Delivery) combined with item category groups like NORM set to item category TANN. The key configuration ties the pricing procedure to a zero-value condition type like RVAA01 with requirement 024, ensuring no net price is calculated regardless of material master price. The leadership value is eliminating unauthorized revenue leakage and maintaining strict audit trails for promotional inventory write-offs. Next, we will audit all user roles assigned to transaction VA01 to restrict access to free-of-charge document types. Trap: Relying on manual user discipline instead of role authorization and pricing routines to control free deliveries.
panel_qa.trap: Relying on manual user discipline instead of role authorization and pricing routines to control free deliveries.

panel_qa.question: What is the financial accounting impact of subsequent deliveries free-of-charge originating from customer returns, and how do we ensure correct cost posting?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: Subsequent deliveries free-of-charge replace damaged or incorrect goods without issuing a credit memo, requiring precise accounting segregation. SAP handles this through billing type F2 (or specialized billing blocks) mapped to specific SD account determination keys using transaction VKOA. The system posts the cost of goods sold to a designated complaint or warranty expense account rather than standard cost of sales. The leadership value is accurate categorization of quality costs on the P&L statement, providing visibility into the true cost of operational defects. Next, we will review the account determination tables in transaction VKOA to verify GL account assignments for movement type 653. Trap: Assuming free-of-charge deliveries bypass accounting entirely because no customer invoice is generated.
panel_qa.trap: Assuming free-of-charge deliveries bypass accounting entirely because no customer invoice is generated.

panel_qa.question: How does the Subsequent Delivery Free-of-Charge integrate with the Returns and Complaints process in SAP S/4HANA?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: Subsequent deliveries free-of-charge integrate seamlessly as follow-on documents from a preceding returns order or customer complaint notification. SAP links these via copying control defined in transaction VTFL between the returns delivery or credit memo request and the subsequent delivery document. The configuration ensures that reference quantities are validated against the original invoiced quantity to prevent over-delivery of replacement stock. The leadership value is streamlined customer service operations and automated traceability from initial complaint to final replacement delivery. Next, we will configure copy control requirement routines to enforce strict quantity validation limits. Trap: Creating independent free-of-charge orders manually for returns without a preceding reference document, breaking audit traceability.

panel_qa.question: How do we manage statutory tax reporting and value-added tax (VAT) obligations for goods shipped free of charge across international borders?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: Free-of-charge shipments of physical goods still carry regulatory and tax reporting obligations despite generating zero commercial revenue. SAP addresses this through tax determination logic in pricing procedure RVX000 using condition types like UTX1, calculating tax based on the material's taxable value or cost price rather than net invoice value. The key configuration involves setting up tax classification in the material master and customer master to trigger proper reporting on Intrastat and local tax returns. The leadership value is full compliance with local tax authorities, avoiding severe penalties for undeclared cross-border stock movements. Next, we will test tax calculation routines for intercompany free-of-charge shipments in the quality environment. Trap: Leaving tax condition types unassigned in free-of-charge pricing procedures, leading to compliance failures during tax audits.

panel_qa.question: What inventory valuation and stock management controls apply when executing large-scale promotional free-of-charge campaigns?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: Large promotional campaigns require dedicated stock allocation to prevent operational stockouts for paying customers. SAP manages this by utilizing special stock indicators or separate storage locations driven by schedule line categories like CN, which trigger goods issue movement type 621 (Delivery free of charge). The key configuration ensures that requirement type planning takes promotional demand into account without polluting standard sales forecasting metrics. The leadership value is optimized inventory holding costs and protected fulfillment rates for revenue-generating orders. Next, we will refine MRP group parameters in transaction MM02 to separate promotional demand from forecast calculations. Trap: Using standard sales schedule lines for promotions, which skorts demand planning and misleads procurement forecasts.

panel_qa.how_to_answer: Legacy custom tables and programs for sample distribution introduce maintenance overhead and upgrade risks in S/4HANA. SAP provides standard sales document type FD with item category TANN out of the box, supporting complete end-to-end processing from order to delivery and cost posting. The key configuration involves mapping legacy sample reason codes to standard SD reason for ordering fields and implementing standard output determination for delivery notes. The leadership value is reduced total cost of ownership through standard code maintenance and streamlined system upgrades. doc_flow.what: Sales document type FD records the promotional or warranty request without commercial revenue. Orders initiated via VA01 drive downstream logistics without creating a billing due list entry.
Delivery type LF is generated against sales order type FD to initiate picking and shipping operations. Outbound delivery coordinates stock removal for zero-value fulfillment.
Goods issue posting via movement type 631 removes stock from unrestricted-use inventory and posts inventory reduction to a marketing or promotional expense account.

doc_flow.what: The sales quotation records the customer's initial inquiry and pricing terms, serving as the commercial baseline for the subsequent free-of-charge delivery.
The sales order type FD is created with reference to the quotation, utilizing item category TBN and schedule line category CN to drive zero-dollar pricing.
The shipping department creates outbound delivery document LF from the sales order to initiate picking, packing, and staging for promotional or sample inventory.
Posting goods issue with movement type 631 reduces unrestricted stock and posts the inventory cost to a marketing or promotional expense account without creating a billing liability.
Attempting to create a billing document confirms that document type FD is not relevant for billing, correctly preventing any customer invoice generation.
